[quote=dhornaper;60514495][B]Fereydun Khan - President For Life[/b]

The plebiscite to declare Fereydun Khan President for life was little more than lipservice to the notion of Dhornaper as still being a democracy, reminiscent of Ayub Khan, the founder of the republic. The plebsicite had more to do with granting Fereydun Khan's dictatorship a veneer of legitimacy as did Ayub Khan's, a hundred years ago.

The media and propaganda guaranteed a yes vote from most of the public. In fact, the most influential Ayatollah of the country openly declared that he supports it, after the government had announced that several historical mosques would be renovated.

The results were speedily calculated and, as with the plebiscite for a new constitution, roundly falsified. The vote tally read 20,428,572 votes in favor and 79,395 votes against, double the number of votes in favor from the constitution but only a 50% increase in the number of votes against. Despite the enormous falsification of the plebiscite, it would have been unnecessary anyway as the population generally supported Fereydun Khan and, even those that didn't, had no choice but to vote in favor for a lack of any real political opposition.

The Senate officiated the results and sent a delegation to President Khan to congratulate him and award the honor with an escort of shamshir wielding Presidential guardsmen. Fereydun Khan was in the middle of a meeting with his Treasury Ministry, one of the few senior civil servants retained from the pre-coup days of real democracy; the meeting was duly suspended. The leader of the delegation read a prepared statement:

"The people and Senate of Dhornaper proclaims you, Fereydun Khan, as President for Life."

Fereydun Khan responded with an equally prepared and rehearsed statement:

"The people have put their confidence in me and I will continue to make the sacrifice of serving them. The prosperity of Dhornaper will be secured against the uncertainties of the future and fate. I have restored justice, order, and tranquility for the nation and I will continue to defend it. With this honor granted to me, I am, from this moment onwards, equal to all other sovereigns of all types since even kings and emperors can only rule for their own lifetime."[/quote]

So you come to seek out our position, and establish an ally on a continent which is against your ideology, he nodded, Indeed, the government here has noted the rapidity with which your old government fell, and the backers of your revolution, as noted by the chairman earlier we hold no official position yet, however, I am sure that is to change by the end of tonight,

The cardinal finished speaking and looked at the vice-chairman, who spoke then,
The party thusfar is currently opposed to violent revolt or complete overthrow, as you know we believe in the technocratic revolution, where societal progress eliminates the need for the bourgeois to play a major role in matters, the role of the party is to educate and effectively aide through whatever means the eventual dissolution of the bourgeois through the provisions of freedom and the expansion of education, stated Villiard.[/quote]
"The revolution is not something immediately tangible in the mind, Comrade Rochambeau. We can't presume that the ways of the old still exist today." Lo Pilato replied. "When the neo-imperialists think of revolution, they think of anarchy in the streets, cars set alight, and men storming into the government palaces with guillotines at the ready. They think of a small subset of a greater population, who imposes itself upon the nation at the tip of a sword, and who must continue to do so lest they forsake their gains to the counter-revolution. But the revolution can be peaceful, as in Sanguivallis, whereupon the party did not abolish the bourgeois government but instead coopted it, and is now systematically dismantling it in the triumphant advance to communism. We do not condemn your government for not undertaking violence, because violence is not the singular course of action, but we nevertheless believe that more can be done to protect your state from the neo-imperialism that surrounds us."

"Like earning money!" Terrasi conjectured, speaking in a voice just a [i]little[/i] bit too loud for the inside of a car. "If your communist party rests itself on minimum programs, then I believe Sanguivallis has everything you could possibly need! Our dearest ally in the east, Qianxun, has been making wonderful advances in the field of socialist economic policy. That said, we doubt their ability to compete in Elseyran markets especially thanks to their recent commitments in Astanir. Sanguinian steelmaking is among the finest in the continent, you know? Imagine the things collaborative research and development could accomplish if our respective countries could fix tariffs and corporate tax to competitive rates? Oh, and the food too! Imagine the profits we could be raking in if we collaborating on rules of origin agreements for our dairy farms and vineyards?"

Terrasi rapid-fired proposal after proposal after proposal. At a glance, she seemed more like a Vespurian venture capitalist than a Sanguinian socialist. Though, given the precarious situation that the Sanguinian economy had been facing until recently, it probably makes sense why Pio Graci had appointed her, with Lo Pilato seemingly just in attendance to ensure ideological discipline.

"Though, we can discuss these terms when the time is right, Comrade Villiard, Rochambeau." Lo Pilato calmly added. "For now though, I feel it more prudent we enjoy whatever pleasantries that your good government might have prepared for us. Comrade Terrasi?"

"Oh. Uh, yeah." Terrasi responded. "Whoops, sorry. I got carried away for a second..."

Villiard seemed ready to respond to the philosophical angle of the sanguinans, but was stopped by a simple motion from the cardinal, for they had come near to where they were supposed to arrive.

Indeed we shall discuss these terms, but with more proficiently minded people who know the details of trade and negotiation, now look, we arrive! He said.

[i]Hurrah for our division,
May it soon be called to go,
To add its strength to those who have advanced to meet the foe.
Oh bless it, for we know right well,
Wherever it may be,
Twill never fail to honor our great army of the free![/i]

On the 17th of April, 1953, a man stands impatient. The person he was waiting for was supposed to be here an hour ago, and he is getting nervous. Will this truly succeed? But he wipes doubt from his mind. The incompetence cant go on any longer, he must do this for the good of all. Finally, he hears people remark about vehicles approaching the building. Its them.

Stepping out of the central vehicle, is the man who has been causing such a fuss. King Zidan II, on his way to the central committee in order to pass yet another law, which, in the man's mind, will ruin the nation more than it has already been. Those in Elyser and Vespuria have influenced the king too much, and action must be taken.

As the king and his guards walk up the long staircase, he answers questions from reporters and onlookers the best he can while still making good time to the entrance. Now is the chance, the time to strike. Ripping the ancient pistol from its hiding place inside his coat, the man thrusts his arm outwards towards the king as he looks away, trying to answer some newsman.

He pulls the trigger. The bang is heard from inside the crowd, and people run. The bodyguards quickly huddle around the king, doing their best to identify where the shot was from. But the bullet never reached the king. The ancient pistol had exploded in the assassins hand, as the poor upkeep paired with an overloaded homemade bullet caused the weapon to malfunction catastrophically, mauling his hand and sending shrapnel into his face.

The king is ushered back to his motorcade and is secure for now. The news of such an attempt rocks the nation, and finally breaks the tension that has been building for so long. The majority of the military, under General Abu al-Sharif, would quickly mobilize and center itself around the Eastern Army Command, creating an open rebellion to the kings power, the Sabrati Revolutionary Union.

In the west, where outside influence has been much more, launched into a reactionary revolution. While groups were unorganized, they used meetings and agreements to formalize into one as the Democratic Front.

In the middle of it all, was the king and his family, the House of al-Mahdin. Using their relatively central place in all of this, those still loyal massed around the southern center of the nation to create a bulwark as well as a potential fallback route to the Lavian border.

The board is set, the game ready. [/spoiler]

[b][i]36 miles outside the city of Eluoja, 7:48, West Elseyran Time[/i][/b]

On the [i]GNV Sotavasarasat[/i] sat a Captain Tapio, reading a book in his Captains Quarters. Outside, it snowed gently upon Gythenas waters, a sign of winters recession and the coming of the months of sunlight. He looked up from his book and gazed into the outside.

How gently the waters moved and swayed with spirit, almost as if alive and carrying the ship across the seas with its grace. Said waters were Gythenas bane and benefit, taking people across the waters while cracking its whip across the coast from time to time.

Suddenly, commotion was heard from below Tapios deck, sounding akin to stomping and rushed movements. Tapio stood up and looked out his front-view window down to bow side.

He didnt see much, just the front of the ship and the pale blue sea. He was about to sit back down to his book when he heard louder banging from under the deck. He froze for a solid 20 seconds, listening in for more noises, before deciding to walk to the door to check what was up.

All of a sudden, Tapios own Coast Guard troops were rushing up the stairs and up to his quarters. Tapio was quickly outmatched and put his hands up as the men burst through the door, aiming their assault rifles at their captain and reorganizing. One of the soldiers piped up:
Surrender control of the vessel immediately and we will let the rest of the crew and you leave with your lives. Make your choice.

Tapio was in shock, thinking, [i]what? Why are my troops going against my command? What is happening in Gythena to cause such a rebellion? Did we get raided by pirates?[/i] Nevertheless, he conceded to the soldiers commands and gave control of the ship to them. The soldiers quickly took to the command board and began handing the ship.

Where are we headed now?
Eluoja. They wont be expecting our arrival, the ships at harbor will be easy targets. If the men on the Raivoa are successful, we will tell them we are headed there
Dont. Fire. At the ships. Some of those are foreign property and we cant afford to make enemies out of anyone if we want any of our efforts to go anywhere. Besides, the element of surprise might be enough considering were have at least one ship suddenly aiming at their port.

Tapio simply sat in his chair, surrounded by armed men ready to fire at any moment, while he contemplated it all.
[i]Pyhä, what is going on[/i]
He simply sat there in his chair, surrounded by armed men ready to fire at any moment. He looked at the future with confusion and concern, as the ship turned around and prepared its arsenal.

[quote=skullsbrough;60492603]Landing in his Wolo-57. A small private aircraft that the royalists previously enjoyed for diplomatic missions, but now had been seized for the republicans for in General Government travel. Klos Reuter would be looking through his "script," per se. Really, it was just a list of items that both Muller and Fuelenger had asked, or demanded that he speak to the Livonians about. These were, in order of importance to him at least: Stabilization of Relations Military Access, Informing them of the plans to seize the islands, naval equipment acquisitions, including a Destroyer and an Amphibious assault ship. And finally, an arms deal for buying and or licensing more ground equipment. Nervously, he would step out of the aircarft onto the tarmac below, escorted by members of the Internal Revolutionary Guard, and taken to car that had been delivered for his usage before hand, the driver would take him to the meeting location. Looking upon the place it would be a reminder of not only the luxury of Vespurias, but the luxury that he had seen across pre-war floueschia. 

"The view is beautiful here." He says to himself aloud, reminiscing when he was just a simple diplomat, who could use his free travel and acess to an aircraft to travel across Erene. 

He waits outside of the building to meet with the Lavian President and the other government personnel whom he was there to meet with. In the meantime, he would take some more time to run through his notes and conversation topics one more time, to hopefully make sure he doesn't slip up during the meeting.[/quote]

[spoiler=[b]The Meeting #1[/b]]

In the middle of pulling a sheet with information from its grey folder, Reuter hears someone clear their throat in front of him. Looking up, a blue and white uniformed guard stands before him with an expectant look. Quickly putting the paper back in its place, he, along with the small group of guards with him are escorted into the chateau.

Walking over its polished wood floors, he takes a second to observe the decor. Its a good way to gauge who youre about to meet. The halls were modest yet somehow rich, decorated with a few paintings and objects here and there, and the main rooms were all open to each other. Along with the large windows, it gave the house a very nice feel, one Reuter hoped would transition into the meeting. 

After being led for a short time, the guard would stop just before the entrance to a small meeting room, with the balcony doors to the room open. Walking in, Reuter would hear the sliding doors of the room close behind him. This was most likely to keep the meeting mostly private, but the paranoia of the revolutionaries had messed with his brain. Even though they had recently appointed him, there was still a little voice in the back of his head telling him that the revolutionaries could turn on a dime against him. He didn't have to worry about that here though. The meeting would go smoothly as planned and his government would love him for securing a national partner and naval assets. 

A chair could be heard moving on the balcony, and a somewhat older middle aged man appeared from the balcony, wearing what appeared to be a dress uniform. This should be David Witstrom, the Livonian Minister of Defence. Our guest is here! Witstrom yelled over his shoulder to others apparently on the balcony before turning back to Reuter. Come friend, we shall talk over wine. 

Without missing a beat, Witstrom walked off back to the balcony, Reuter following close behind. Two more men were sitting on chairs overlooking the vineyard below, one of them being Wallace H. Achebe, however the other isnt recognizable to him. This man wasnt in the information for the meeting, and that makes him feel uneasy.

You okay? The unnamed man asks, raising an eyebrow at Reuter, interrupting his train of worry. Yes, dont worry for me. He would quickly say before taking a seat. Reaching for the chilled bottle of wine to fill himself a glass, a loud screech breaks the silence as something passes over the chateau. The unknown man speaks again. Airbase is the only downside of this place. Those flyboys keep those HALTR aircraft running constantly as of recent he pauses for a second, glancing at Reuter like he was about to say something he wouldnt want the diplomat to hear. 

Achebe broke the awkward silence. Ah, everyone is here and has a full glass. Now, let's get down to what we are here for. Would you mind informing the others of what business we have together? [/spoiler]

[Spoiler=Back Before Summer]
"You will be back right?!" Sophie said, standing on the tarmac, the loud chaos in the background, composed of the loud roars of the Wolo Trab-20s and Trab-30s preparing for take off or idling, men and women of the Fallschirmjäger running around the tarmac, or their transports being loaded into the aircraft. All the busyness of an airbase preparing for one of the largest operations undertaken by the Fallschirmjäger in their history, mostly drowning out her rather quiet voice. 

Marc looked at his sister and his parents, like many in the Fallschirmjäger, families were given access to the base to be able to wave of and speak there family brothers, sisters, fathers, and mothers as they left the base

"Of course, Sophie. I'll be back before summer even starts. You probably won't even notice I'm gone." He says with a smile, looking behind him to see that his transport is about to be ready to leave. His parents look at him with concern. 

"Where are you even going, Marc? Have they told you?", His mother Claire says

Marc looks back 

"You know I can't tell you that, mother. But they said it's not far. It isn't nevonia" He says, looking back to see his commander beginning to read of names, he needs to join formation soon

His father, Jean looks at him, he was a Fallschirmjäger back in his youth, long retired now.

"Just don't die. Okay Marc?" He says, with a firm tone.

"I won't. I didn't die during the revolution. Did I?" Marc replies

He hears his commander call his name. He knows its time

"Look. I love you guys. I really do. I will be able to talk to you guys on the phone in a week, okay?"

He says, walking away towards his commander, during the briefing, they said he will be back in late May or early June when they are rotated off the island and regulars arrive. Back before summer, he repeated to himself as he stepped into formation, and then into the transport.[/Spoiler]

[Spoiler=Preperation for Operation Amity]Gonthier Fuelenger had long coveted the Aruelen Island chain. There strategic location as an observation post in not only a major sea dividing Erene's four major continents, but also against Vespurias and other Continental Rivals, and there known to have potentially trillion-dollar oil extraction potential. It was his firm belief that taking the islands would only be an economic and military boon for the fledgling republic, and it was his dream to see Floueschia turn from a second-rate military power to a great power on the global stage. And taking these islands would hopefully be the first part of that. And best of all, the islands were likely uninhabited. The Ieweschte Revolutionär Kommando, on the other hand, both hated and feared actually executing his plan. Fuelenger plans, while clearly showing his "competence" in drawing up military operations...had a fundamental defect. Floueschia didn't have a navy. The Royal Navy had fled kommend upon catching wind of the massacres in Vëlvetel. Worst still, the marines had gone with them. Leaving Floueschia without a way to amphibious operation. No worries, according to fuelenger. The Fallschirmjäger, which along with Bierg Infanterie had sided with the revolution. Meaning there were two special forces branches readily available to carry out the operation. 

The IRK confronted Muller and Fuelenger that such an operation would basically be impossible for the National People's Army to carry out, pointing out their complete lack of a functional navy beyond a handful of submarines, some of which had been sabotaged by royalists and were inoperable. And a partially destroyed cruiser that had been scuttled by the royalists in front of Komend's Major Port to prevent the republicans from using it for some time. Although the National People's Army Engineering Corp had successfully refloated the ship and had it towed to Komend Naval Yards, the cruiser was 1. From the 70s, specifically a "Gaberiala Class Heavy Cruiser" 2. Most of its weapon systems had been preeminently sabotaged, and 3. Had a massive gapping hull where its ammunition storage once was, most of the superstructure had been destroyed. It would take approximately 2 years to return it to functional services, and the IRK had already written it off as a loss. On top of this, the islands were decently far away from military supply, meaning each trip of supply to the islands for at least the first operation would need extensive amounts of fueling and logistics that could potentially take away from military operations in Nevonia. And lastly, it's likely that there would be ongoing storms and adverse sea conditions, making any landing, especially from the air, a dangerous task anyway. Fuelenger blew off the IRK. And Müller, who had already committed to the operation, simply told them to work with what they could.

The IRK started with the most obvious issue: the lack of the navy. Fuelenger's and Reuter's overtures to Livonia were currently ongoing, and would not be ready by the set date of the invasion. Meaning that the IRK would, for now, have to look to alternatives.  Those alternatives came in the case of 3 cargo ships formerly belonging to the Royal Merchant Marine Company, now under the custody of the Department of the Interior. The Newest Revolutionär Kommando, acting on behalf of the Marine Kräften's non-existent military, officially requisitioned the ships. They were in a convenient spot aswell, sitting in Komend's Civilian piers awaiting buyers. They were towed to Komend's naval yards, and Stol & Stroum Schëffsbau was given a 60 million contract to begin their conversion, each of them being around 52,000 tons, more than enough for the role they were to be given.

Starting with the MV Royal Collector, now renamed to the NVMKS Victory was to be reconfigured into a troopship, with its cargoholds being replaced with prefabricated bunk departments, its hull reinforced with steel plating and being armed with light, cold war era anti-aircraft guns taken from the stockpile, its hull was then painted a dull grey to fit its new role. Then the MV McSulivan, now renamed into the NVMKS Revolution, which was converted into a mobile fire support ship, doubling as a supply and transport ship, its cargo holds would be reconfigured to hold military equipment, with one being dedicated to ammunition. 10 155mm Howitzers would be placed atop its deck, its deck also being reinforced to carry the weight. And lastly, the MV Royal, now the NVMKS Liberty, would be converted into a helicopter carrier and mobile hospital, its top deck being strengthened to carry around 10 helicopters, 5 would be dedicated to medical evacuations, and 5 to mobile fire support. Additionally, its cargo holds would be converted into hospitals. With transports acquired, the IRK moved onto the actual operational planning.

Operation Amity was the first of these operations that would be carried out by Fallschirmjäger and the Bierg Infanterie, and covered the island of Mondsei, the smallest island in the chain. And its specifics would be mildly concerning to the IRK at best. The Fallschirmjäger, the most elite division in the National People's Army, were to be first on the island. Fuelenger's specifications indicated that the Fallschirmjäger's role would be to essentially act as marines, deploy from the air, and land on the beaches of the islands. Quickly securing them. They would set up a perimeter around the beach and clear out vegetation for one week. The IRK estimated that it would take about 22 Heavy Lift aircraft and 12 hours to take the battalion from their airbase at Reinsyerl to the island; luckily, they had the aircraft ready. The Royalist had bought almost 50 for the Fallschirmjäger from Wolo starting in the 2000s, and by the time of the revolution, all but 20 had been delivered. Still, this only left 10 in reserve, as it would take Wolo another year or two to fulfill the order. After the 12-hour flight, the Fallschirmjäger would land on the islands within a time span of 20 minutes, to avoid international attention, it was decided that the initial landings would occur at midnight. At the same time that the planes left, however, the Mountain Division and their equipment, aboard the Revolution, Liberty, and Victory would leave port, escorted by 3 submarines to the islands.

The Bierg Infanterie's job was to land on the secured beachhead, and then spread out across the island, occupying the remainder and preparing it for regular infantry and army engineers to begin clearing out the island for the construction of an impromptu military base for operations across the remainder of the islands. Taking Mondsei would also formalize Floueschia's claim to the region internationally. Mondesi would hopefully be secured by early June if the operation went to plan, and by late July if not. With everything in place, the first aircraft would leave Reinsyerl field, en route to the islands on the 12th of May, 2026.

[b]Mondesi, First Day of Operation Amity[/b]
[Spoiler=Operation Amity pt2]
Marc would look anxiously at his squad mates, they were to be the second squad out of the aircraft. He notices that the rest of his squad are smiling, laughing, telling jokes among themselves, while their commander is simply taking a smoke. Then he hears it, the automated intercom alarm

"Alarm! Alarm! At attention! We have confirmation from HQ back at Reinsyerl. We are to begin landing operations. Prepare to dive, make all final checks, especially your weapons and parachutes. To armored crews, your equipment will be waiting for you on the beach, it's already been dropped by the supply craft who are now back on their way to Reinsyerl, and all other aircraft that are not ourselves as well. This means you will be the last on the island. We lost contact with the group on the ground but we assume that it will be restored shortly. The jump doors will open in...1 minute. Goodluck Fallschirmjäger, be safe.  "

The intercom goes out, he sees everyone around him jump up and begin grabbing parashoots and their weapons. He does so as well, he double-checks both his main parachute and his backup parashoot, then triple-checks it. The first squad lines up at the jump door as it slowly creeps open. They leap from the jump doors into the darkness below. Marc had almost forgotten that these were night landings. His squad lines up, his Captain, Rubert Edrich out of the plane first, followed by his squad mates, including his long-time friend Robert Kerger. He is the last out, gliding through the air he hears a sudden infernal screech that almost defends him, glances back at his plane. And suddenly, with no warning he sees a blue flash that smacks into the plane, destroying it instantly, in panic he throws up his shot early, accidentally knocking his radio, which he had forgotten to secure.

He comes to the earth in a clearing with the rest of his squad; the explosion of the aircraft had distracted them from the fact that the aircraft had dropped them in the wrong place. 

"Well, F*ck this. Right?"

Robert says, looking into the wilderness that surrounds them on all sides

"Do we even know where the hell we are right now? Or are we just lost? And what the dam plane? What the hell was that?"

Marc looks around and notices a perfectly cut tree stump right by them. Actually, looking around, there are a lot of them in this clearing. "More relevantly. Who the hell cut this wood? These islands are uninhabited, right, Captain?"

Captain Edrich looks around confused. He had been specifically told that nobody lived on these islands 

"Well. Yeah. But either way, we should get moving. It's going to be long-"

Suddenly, Captain Edrich is stabbed straight through the chest by a long black object, killing him instantly. Whatever did it tosses him into a nearby tree, the hulking, black fox-like monstrosity behind it, standing in front of them, charges at one of the other paratroopers, Robert, now in command screams 

"F*CK F*CK, SHOOT IT. JUST SHOOT IT"

A haze of bullets screams towards the monster as the paratrooper, it was charging, gets pounced to the ground and killed, Robert, marc and the last remaining paratrooper after realizing they have dumped about 3 full mags between the 3 of them and it not seeming effected at all decide to simply run into the forest, the screams of whatever it was chasing them through it violently. The foliage of the forest, now clearly a jungle, just gets deeper and deeper until mobility becomes practically impossible. Eventually, Marc stops moving, tired from running for what dam near must have been a straight 10 or so minutes.

"Robert?" He says, no response, he must have been separated, he thought. 

"Goddammit. God F*CKING dammit. ROBERT? ANYONE?"

He looks around to try to gain awareness of his surroundings, nothing, just the noise of wildlife going through the trees, crickets chirping, and a stream that must have been somewhere nearby. However, he smells something, smoke, burnt rubber. He follows the scent to the stream, where he sees one of the Fallschirmjäger's APCs almost completely destroyed. In its dead center, it looked like something had torn straight through the hull. He called out again, but no response. Whatever happened, the crew clearly wasn't around anymore, then he remembered. The APCs had radios, which could potentially allow them to contact other Fallschirmjäger units and attempt to regroup. Entering the APC through the hole, the entire thing had been completely ravaged, even when he found the radio it was destroyed. He was trapped. Seeing no other option, he decided to camp out in the APC until morning.[/spoiler]

[Spoiler=Operation Amity pt2]
The landings were a complete disaster. After just one night of fighting on the islands, 503 of the 1,200 men who landed on the island were either dead, severely injured, or missing in action. The battered and bloodied remnants of the 1st Fallschirmjäger Batailloun would regroup and reassemble themselves on the target beach, operationally called "Diamond beach". Unknown to the Stase, the IRK, and Fuelenger, the islands were not uninhabited, not in the slightest. In fact, the primary residents of these islands were extremely aggressive, sadistic, and territorial wildlife. While sizes varied, one thing did not. They were impractically invulnerable to the small arms ammunition that the Fallschirmjäger had brought with them, especially the larger creatures. The main threat of these were fox-like, extremely fast, and extremely deadly creatures that the Fallschirmjäger troops on the island simply named the "Kobre" a Nevonian term loosely translating to "demon". Other wildlife included extremely large insectoids, most of the time flying creatures that were extremely venomous. Fallschirmjäger medics, the ones that were left at least, had no ability to treat the toxin that they would inflict on infected paratroopers. The island's terrain and climate, which was thick jungle-like forests and foggy beaches, also presented significant challenges for the Fallschirmjäger as it made it extremely hard to search the island for lost squads or individual members. Still however. The Fallschirmjäger had completed its mission, with fortifications in the form of trenches and wooden walls being established, forming a perimeter, and a stable beachhead on Diamond Beach...Now they just had to hold it, reinforcements were a week away.

When Fuelenger received a report from the 1st Battalion's Commander, Erin Reinhard, on the situation on the ground he was horrified. And horrified even more to present Muller with the shocking danger he had put a thousand men into, and the practical massacre of one of Floueschia's best army units. Müller, upon being briefed on the situation by members of the Stase and IRK, would reportedly end the meeting early and not be seen for the remainder of the day, suffering a breakdown from the sheer human cost of Fuelenger's mistake. To save face, Fuelenger, with the permission of the IRK and Muller, ordered the immediate reinforcement of the 1st Battalion with the 2nd Battalion of the Fallschirmjäger. Who, with prior knowledge of the dangers, took extra precautions and landed almost completely intact 48 hours after the initial landings, finding the 1st battalion almost completely shattered, many squads in the battalion were left without leadership. 2nd Battalion Commander, Mia Heinz would take command of the Fallschirmjäger on the island and begin reorganizing the 1st battalion, which was rotated off defensive duties of the beachhead. The 2nd Battalion, taking their place, would begin to expand the defensive perimeter to cover Gold and Silver beaches as well. With the arrival of the 2nd Battalion also came their small tank unit, giving the Fallschirmjäger extra firepower to hold off the wildlife of the island for another 5 days. 

Finally, on Tuesday, May 19th, almost 7 days since the 1st battalion landed on the island. The main fleet arrived, coming ashore, General François Mertes, leading the 1. Biergdivisioun to the joy of the beleaguered Fallschirmjäger would rotate both battalions of defensive duties, helicopters and boats would ferry the wounded, sick, and tired back to the NVMKS Victory or NVMKS Liberty. While the NVMKS would begin to act as a command ship, the command of both battalions and the Berig Division would be transferred there and begin operating. One day after the arrival of the main force. Helicopters began to scour the island for signs of 1st Battalion survivors; they found barely a handful; the thickness of the jungle didn't allow them to see through to the island's surface, while the size of the island made it risky to go for long periods of time flying around the island.

[b]Islanders[/b]
[Spoiler=Islanders pt1]
Marc wakes up. He had hoped it was all a bad dream, maybe he had fallen asleep on the aircraft. But no, when he woke up, his worst fears had been confirmed. He was still in the burnt-out APC that he had cowered in for the night. However, something wasn't right. He could feel it. Getting up, he would look around the APC, checking every nook, cranny, and seat for answers to his suspicions, but it was nothing, nothing but the quiet hymn of the sun and the water gently moving through the creek. Then he felt his back. His gun was gone. In fact, all of the guns were gone from the gun rack in the APC. 

"No no no no..." He would slowly repeat to himself as he looked for his assault rifle. The only hope he had of actually defending himself in this situation. But it was gone. Something had come through last night; it must have. 

He went for his holster, his side arm. Was thankfully still there. This was all he had now. He had to make it back to base.

"Don't die."

 He sighs, stepping out of the APC, and he would be greeted by the same surroundings that he had seen in the morning: thick foliage. His only directive now was to make it to Diamond Beach. Looking to his right, he would see the corpse of one of the APC crew in the stream; the poor guy had been stabbed by something while trying to flee the scene. He looked down, the mud had mostly preserved his original steps. He decides to follow the footprints in the mud, back through the foliage of the island. Stopping whenever he heard even the quietest sign of movement. He would eventually be able to make it back to the clearing. The bodies of his commander and fellow paratrooper were gone, clearly having been dragged further into the forest. Looking around, he manages to find his commander's light machine gun and radio, picking both up he would go to sit on a stump to call for help.

"Hello? Hello! This is Marc Hoffman! 1st Batal-"

He notices the radio isn't working, he also notices rumbling in the bush, he immediately turns his light machine gun in the direction and opens fire, whatever it was slumps to the floor with ease, much different from what he experienced earlier. Approaching it and dragging whatever it was out of the bush. It seems to be a...Person?

[Spoiler=Islanders pt2]
By May 23rd, the First Battalion had been fully reorganized. It came out of the first landing a bloodied mess, but still a capable fighting force ready for the next stage of the campaign. At the same time, the original plan was to completely rotate the Fallschirmjäger off the island. The IRK had become increasingly concerned that the Mountaineers would not be able to take the entire island completely on their own. And therefore, the 1st and 2nd Battalions were to fight with the mountaineers to fully occupy the island. Firstly, General François Mertes would take control of all three army units on the island, forming Army Group "Mondesi" a day before the operation began. Now in direct command, and having learned from the mistakes of the initial landing, he ordered the Army Group to wait until the morning of the 25th to begin offensive operations. Equipped with flame throwers delivered in mass by air through the following days, the 1st Battalion was to be the first back into the jungles of the island, meant to burn paths through the thick jungles. They would be closely followed by armored forces that would fight with them through the jungles.

One hour into the operation, a group of first battalion paratroopers and mountain division IFVs discovered roads, although mostly just dirt paths through the jungle. Having forced their way to the jungle. These roads seemed mostly cleared of hostiles already. Some even led back to Diamond Beach, although the entrances to these roads were almost intentionally covered from view by more brush. This allowed a detachment of the 1st battalion, which included all of the battalion's remaining APCs and a borrowed tank from Second Battalion, to penetrate far deeper into the island than had been done in the previous days, almost without contest. Meanwhile, those who were not lucky enough to be ordered down the roads and had to burn their way through the jungles would enjoy hefty fire support from both helicopters, using rockets and machine gun fire to obliterate the more dangerous form of wildlife on the island. And coastal fire support, as the howitzers on the Revolution could almost completely cover the entire northern half of the island. Fire support would mostly consist of regular ammunition; however, in desperate situations would also include shells filled with mustard and chlorine gas. Despite this, it took another 2 days to clear out most of the northern half of the island. And casualties had been heavy, the creatures of the islands were still extremely deadly even with all of the support the forces of the National People's Army had.

The armored task force on the road, in the middle of the night on May 25th, reported to command that they had come into contact with an "irregular village" on the island. As the armored task force dismounted and entered the village. They were welcomed warmly. With no sense of hostility from the confused villagers. The armored task force was instead presented with over 67 men from the 1st Battalion, whom the villagers had gone out of their way to rescue from across the northern half of the island. Most of them were severely injured; however, the villagers' medical treatments had kept them stable. General François Mertes immediately ordered that he be taken to the village by helicopter, along with him or vocalist, magic users within the mountaineers who would be able to translate the villagers' language. Along with him, he took all of the medical evacuation helicopters to be able to evacuate the 67 men back to the NVMKS Victory for immediate medical treatment. After sitting down with the village's leaders, they were told that over 20 settlements like it existed across the island. The island was technically claimed by a larger confederation that was mostly centered on the largest island in the chain. However, they had lost contact shortly before the NVA had landed on the island. And would be happy to assist the NVA in their campaign to secure the island so long as their sovereignty was respected. While the general informed them that he had no such authority, he would ensure his superiors at least heard their pleas for what they had done for the men of the 1st battalion.

It would take another 4 weeks of combat to fully secure the aboveground of the island. On June 26, at 6:37 am, the flag of the republic would be raised above the mountain top of the island, surrounding it, over 50 helmets and other personal items of the 1st battalion. A painful memorial to the now over 557 members of the 1st battalion who were killed, wounded, or missing on the island. However, the island still had vast cave networks in which many of the creatures had either already lived in or fled to, as the aboveground of the island fell. The Mountaineers and the 2nd Battalion were to stay behind on the island and begin clearing out these tunnels. The 1st battalion, however, was done. They were ferried back to the NVMKS Victory and arrived in Komend a week afterwards. They were welcomed with great fanfare in the city and paraded around the city as heroes. The 1st battalion returned to their barracks at Reinsyerl Field and were informed that they would return to the islands for another operation within 2 months, the amount of time it would take to fully rehabilitate the battalion. while the capturing of the islands came at a high price, with almost 1,032 killed, injured, or missing. Fuelenger had his island, and within the coming weeks would order an army engineering brigade ashore, who would begin to expand the roads on the island and begin laying out plans for the construction of air field on Diamond Beach. Fuelenger would put François Mertes directly in charge of administering the island, which would be labeled the "Mondesi Special Administrative Region," and formally annexed by the Fleischian Government in an announcement to the global community using the IA as a form.

François Mertes would first decide to declare the villages no-go zones; no occupation forces were allowed to enter the villages or an area around them without the explicit permission of their elders or ruling councils. He formed an open forum where these villages would be able to communicate with his office directly and issue any protest they had with the ongoing occupation of the island. Although he informed them there was nothing he could do about the annexation, he informed them that they were now protected under the Flouesch Constitution and its "Declaration on the Rights of Man". Meaning that they could also formally protest to the mainland government if needed. And offered tools to do so as needed. The mountaineers would get to work in clearing out tunnels that were an immediate danger to the villages or the base at Diamond Beach. At the same time, the Engineers went around the island and blew up the entrances of any other caves to hopefully trap the abominations below in the caves and allow them to starve out. For the Fallschirmjäger 2nd Battalion, they were simply garrison and patrol forces.[/Spoiler]
